name: Kish (Saul's father)
title: Saul's father and a wealthy Benjaminite
summary: Kish was a wealthy man from the tribe of Benjamin and the father of Saul, Israel's first king. He is known as a mighty warrior and an influential figure in his tribe. His sending of his son Saul to look for lost donkeys indirectly led to Saul's anointing as king.

keyEvents.title: Introduction as Saul's father
keyEvents.description: Kish is presented as a wealthy and powerful man from the tribe of Benjamin, a prominent figure in his community.

keyEvents.title: The Lost Donkeys
keyEvents.description: Kish lost his donkeys and sent his son Saul out to look for them, which led to Saul's meeting with the prophet Samuel.

keyEvents.title: Kish's lineage mentioned
keyEvents.description: Kish is mentioned as part of Saul's lineage when Saul is presented to the people as their new king.

keyEvents.title: Saul's burial at Kish's tomb
keyEvents.description: After Saul's death, his bones and those of his sons were buried in Kish's tomb in Sela, showing the family's burial place and honor.
